newsitem.title: USA: World Bank to approve $800 mln Russia loan - sources.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to approve $800 mln Russia loan - sources.

text.p: The World Bank is set to approve a $800 million loan to back Russia's social reforms when its board meets on Wednesday, monetary sources said.
The loan is part of a $1.7 billion package announced earlier this month.
It will be the biggest loan the World Bank has ever offered to a country in central and eastern Europe and aims to create an appropriate system of social protection.

World Bank President James Wolfensohn has said the bank could lend Russia $10 billion over the next three years, mainly in projects designed to help ease the painful social consequences of economic reform.
This would make the World Bank a bigger lender to Russia than the International Monetary Fund, which is backing Mosow's economic reform program with a $10 billion three-year loan.
Several World Bank loans were approved earlier this month, including a $600 million credit for structural reform.
